construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Wood generating Fire same-polarity — reach as fuel sustaining warmth
candidates.k2_overview: Your Wood moves as the Alchemist: knowledge grown rather than gathered. Understanding grafts onto you slowly and lives, ideas cross-pollinating in ways textbooks never planned. Your learning is a garden with strange hybrids. Tend it privately as you must, then let people taste the fruit. It is stranger and better than you think.
candidates.k2_functional: You think by grafting: splicing distant ideas until something new takes root.

k2_domain_readings.Learning: You learn like an ecosystem: slowly, laterally, everything connecting to everything. Formal courses feel like pots. Give yourself wild ground, mixed sources, and the hybrids will astonish.
k2_domain_readings.Intuition: Your intuition grows on the underside of awareness: a slow mycelium that suddenly fruits an answer. Give questions dormancy. What you cannot force overnight arrives by spring.
k2_domain_readings.Solitude: Your solitude is a greenhouse: ideas need protected warmth before weather. Take the seclusion without guilt. Just transplant finished thoughts outdoors. Gardens are meant to be walked in.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, little soaks in from outside. Your own stores feed you, and hunches fill the gaps where lessons would have gone.

angles.drive: Sensing a thing first comes easier to you than waiting to be told. You sense the pause before an answer, and your guess runs past the words. The mood of a gathering reaches you before anyone has named it.
angles.cost_self: A thing sensed first feels safer than a plain question asked. Since you would rather sense it than be told, what you have half right stays half right. Underneath, you want to be understood without explaining yourself.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone starts telling you something, you sense its direction and answer that. Sensing the point before the words saves you time and costs the other person their own ending. Your quick replies leave their stories half told.

angles.drive: You teach yourself what others take classes in. Being handed an answer never feels like knowing it, and you would rather be self-taught than shown. The self-taught way costs you time, and what you learn by it is the kind that stays.
angles.cost_self: Being self-taught makes the knowing yours. The long way feels more honest than the short, so you spend years on what a teacher would hand you in a day. Part of you would love a guide, and that wish goes unsaid.
angles.cost_others: Teaching yourself means you rarely ask anyone who knows. Working it out alone feels cleaner than owing an answer, so you keep questions private. Friends with skills to share seldom get the pleasure of showing you.

angles.drive: You ask why before you accept how things are done. An answer only feels like yours once you have pulled it apart, and you question the accepted way rather than take it on trust. Your questions turn up the flaw everyone else walked past.
angles.cost_self: Asking why keeps you from settling into any easy answer. You need to see the reason for yourself, and the comfort of simply believing stays out of reach. Each clear answer is paid for with some of your peace.
angles.cost_others: With other people's plans, you ask why before you join in. Taking part only feels honest once the reason holds up for you, and your questions arrive before your help does. Friends get a sharper plan and a slower yes.

friction.define: As a friction, you take in far more than you use. What you know piles up out of sight, because a thing half known feels unsafe to act on.

angles.drive: Thinking a question through means thinking it around, each side first. Being certain weighs more with you than being quick, so you take one more angle rather than decide. You circle a question for weeks that a single choice would have closed.
angles.cost_self: Thinking in circles is your way of never being wrong. One more side feels like care rather than delay, and the choice stays open while you turn it over. You lose the chances that needed an answer this week, one careful lap at a time.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone brings you a question, you think in circles first. Every side counts for more than a usable reply, so you hand over the process instead of a yes. You make them wait through every circle for an answer they needed short.

angles.drive: What you understand, you keep in. Saying a thing out loud makes it ordinary, and you would rather hold an idea unfinished than hand it over half-formed. Keeping it in keeps it yours, and you never learn what it would have become.
angles.cost_self: Keeping it in feels safer than being half understood. The private version stays perfect while the spoken one takes its chances, so you say the smaller idea. You keep the idea safe and lose the one thing you wanted from it, being known.
angles.cost_others: You keep in what your closest people want to know. A held thought feels less exposed than a shared one, and you give silence instead of answers. You leave them guessing at what you think, the one thing they asked you for.

angles.drive: You hide away to think, and the hiding comes before the thinking. Company costs you the thread of an idea, so you would rather be alone with a question than with people and an answer. Hiding away feeds the work and quietly stops feeding you.
angles.cost_self: Hiding away protects what is growing in you. Because time alone feels like rest to you, you hide away rather than go out and keep the quiet past the point it helps. Behind the shut door, you pay in closeness for every hour of quiet.
angles.cost_others: When people who love you reach for you, you hide longer. Being out of reach feels more like safety than absence, and your seat sits empty. On the days that count, you leave them a friend short.

retired_2026-09-20_batch3.fn_reading.catalyst.Perceptive.scene: You told your partner the neighbors were splitting up three months before the moving truck confirmed it, citing only the way they parked. It sounded absurd in March. In June it sounded like surveillance. It was neither. It was the parking, plus attention.

edge.lead: Wood runs through your mind, your growth and your career. It is the far-apart things in your head that fit together, the next you that slips in by a side door, and the shift at work you feel before anyone says it.
